record.summary: Guidelines for the safe, responsible and trustworthy development, deployment and use of generative AI across Egypt's public and private sectors, academia and society, developed under MCIT and approved by the National Council. They address misinformation and deepfakes, hallucinations, bias, privacy, intellectual property and accountability, and expect human validation of outputs, disclosure of AI-generated content by labels or provenance mechanisms such as metadata and watermarking, consent for use of a person's likeness or voice, limits on deepfakes in elections and news, and, for agentic AI, human approval of irreversible or high-risk actions and emergency pause, override and shutdown.
record.notes: Version 1.0, dated March 2026. Besides general guidelines for trustworthy use, it has sections on agentic AI, on deepfakes and lip-sync, which it describes, following international practice, as a high-risk enabling capability, on generative AI in education and scientific research, and on disclosure of generative AI use, with disclosure templates. The guidelines state that they were drafted with the help of generative AI tools and that human authors reviewed and verified all AI-generated text. The Guide to Egypt's National AI Governance Framework (EG-02) lists generative AI guidelines for government and individuals in its Phase 1 agenda.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored: the guidelines PDF (52 pages) from ai.gov.eg, stored 11 Oct 2026 and unchanged when rechecked on 18 Oct 2026. judgment.status_reasoning: Version 1.0 of March 2026, approved by the National Council; principles-based guidance with no stored sign of a newer version. Published (non-binding, current).
judgment.scope_reasoning: National government guidelines on generative AI risks (deepfakes, hallucinations, agentic AI safeguards); in scope with no note.

judgment.topics_reasoning: Unchanged and supported: general-purpose / frontier AI (generative and foundation models, agentic AI), deepfakes & synthetic media (deepfake and lip-sync section), transparency & labelling (disclosure, labels, metadata, watermarking), human oversight (human approval and final decision authority), incident reporting (procedures for incident reporting; rapid reporting of harmful content).
